translations.answer: Use the version containing PR #2022 in 'train.py' to save 'model_vecnormalize.pkl' in the 'run' directory; 'play.py' loads this file from the selected checkpoint directory and sets 'training=False' and 'norm_reward=False', while reading the 'params/agent.yaml' saved during training. If custom scripts lack these steps, normalization stats and policy checkpoint must be saved and loaded together; only loading policy weights is insufficient to reproduce the training input distribution.
translations.applicability: Applies to Isaac Lab SB3 workflows that enable 'normalize_input' or 'normalize_value'; custom directory structures must be adjusted.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and free of conflicts, and there is formal documentation or precise citation of the exact reproduction.
translations.details.attempts.0: The original post states that any SB3 environment can execute the normalize_input/normalize_value reproduction steps and recommended code.
translations.details.attempts.1: PR #2022 simultaneously modifies the save/load paths in 'train.py' and 'play.py'.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Check if 'play' loads the stats from the target checkpoint directory and disables 'training' and 'reward normalization'.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Check if 'play' uses the 'agent.yaml' saved during training, rather than the current default configuration.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use the version containing PR #2022 (merge commit ad14a67); training saves 'model_vecnormalize.pkl', evaluation loads from the corresponding checkpoint directory and sets 'training=False' and 'norm_reward=False'.
translations.details.environments.0: IsaacLab commit 9f1aa4c, Isaac Sim 4.5.0, Ubuntu 22.04.5, RTX 3500 Ada Laptop 12GB, CUDA 12.1, driver 535.230.02.
translations.details.limits.0: The filename and path are bound to the specific Isaac Lab script associated with the PR; custom runners must verify their checkpoint layout.
translations.details.limits.1: No author has upgraded to retest the issue; the closure is primarily due to the merged code and maintenance confirmation.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The SB3 maintainer explicitly confirmed the issue should be fixed by PR #2022, and the issue was subsequently closed; the original author did not post performance numbers after the upgrade.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does play performance degrade and reaccumulate statistics after enabling VecNormalize in SB3 training?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before deployment, verify that policy, VecNormalize stats, agent config, and code commit are treated as a single, non-dismantleable artifact.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Training statistics are not persisted; the evaluation endpoint reinitializes and updates the mean and variance.
translations.details.symptoms.0: train.py does not save normalization statistics; play.py uses a fresh VecNormalize and continues training.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The evaluation normalization distribution is inconsistent with training, and policy performance degrades.
translations.source.locator: IsaacLab #2635 complete reproduction; SB3 maintainer confirms 3004477599; PR #2022
translations.source.title: SB3 play.py must load training VecNormalize stats rather than relearning them.
translations.title: How does Isaac Lab's SB3 play.py avoid relearning VecNormalize stats?
